title: task archive takes no --if-revision, so a guarded edit followed by an archive cannot close its race window
description:
Requested by opum-agent (cross-session, 2026-09-29), from an independent review of opum-ai/opum-agent#1446 (OPAG-799, F1). The request: the operator-request helper retires a record with a guarded `task edit --if-revision` followed by `task archive`; the archive cannot be guarded, so a record that changes between the two steps is still archived. A re-read narrows the window in the helper, but only a guarded archive closes it.

MEASURED on quest-cli dev at d58a8286 and on the installed 0.11.0: `quest help task archive` lists only actor flags -- the "task archive" entry in src/application/command-help.ts carries flags: [...ACTOR_FLAGS] -- and Tasks.archive() in src/application/tasks/tasks.ts takes no revision precondition, routing straight to moveTask(reference, "archive/tasks", operationId). The existing guard is `task edit --if-revision` (QCLI-277), which refuses a stale edit as a conflict; QCLI-374 fixed that refusal to report conflict rather than validation. QCLI-389 tracks a surviving exit-6 edge on the edit path when a stale edit also carries a gone removal target.

DESIRED: `quest task archive <id> --if-revision <revision>` with the semantics edit already has: the precondition is the per-record revision a caller captures from `quest task view --json`; a stale value refuses the archive as a conflict (exit 5) and moves nothing; a current value archives exactly as today.

SCOPE: archive is the measured gap. Whether the other lifecycle moves (complete, pause, start, demote) want the same guard is NOT decided here and is out of this task. No design is decided by the requester.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `quest task archive <id> --if-revision <rev>` is accepted; with the revision captured from `quest task view --json` just before, the archive proceeds as today and relocates the record to `archive/tasks`.
With a stale revision the archive is refused as a conflict -- exit 5 -- and the record is not moved; the refusal is distinguishable from a usage error (exit 2) and a validation error (exit 6).
The revision compared is the same per-record value `quest task view --json` emits and `task edit --if-revision` compares against, so one captured value works for either command.
`quest help task archive` and the machine command registry document the flag.
